chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Abū al-Jawzāʾ, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlwān, from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī, from his forefathers, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم led us in the ẓuhr prayer as five rakʿahs, then he turned away. Some of the people said to him, "O Messenger of Allah, has something been added to the prayer?" He said, "And what is that?" They said, "You led us in five rakʿahs." He said: then he faced the qiblah, said the takbir while seated, then performed two sajdahs in which there was no recitation and no rukuʿ, then he gave salām, and he used to say, "They are the two that humiliate [Shaytan]."

So the proper way regarding this report is that we understand it to mean that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم only performed the two sajdahs because the statement of one person does not produce certainty for him such that he would need to restart the prayer. Rather, it only entails doubt; and whoever doubts an addition, his obligation is to perform the two sajdahs of sahw, as we have explained in our major book. And they are the two that humiliate [Shaytan].

key_terms.الزِّيَادَةِ: an extra addition in the prayer beyond its prescribed form
key_terms.الشَّكَّ: doubt or uncertainty regarding whether an addition occurred
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer under discussion
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةَ: the direction of prayer faced before performing the sajdahs
key_terms.الْمُرْغِمَتَانِ: the two sajdahs described as humiliating Shaytan
key_terms.رَكَعَاتٍ: units of prayer performed in the salat
key_terms.سَجْدَتَيِ السَّهْوِ: the two prostrations of forgetfulness required for such doubt
key_terms.سَجْدَتَيْنِ: the two prostrations performed after the mistake

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone doubts that an extra rakʿah was added to the prayer?
ai.summary: This report discusses a case of apparent addition in salat (prayer), where the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was informed that five rakʿahs had been performed in ẓuhr. The accompanying legal explanation states that since the report of a single person did not establish certainty, the matter was treated as doubt, and the ruling for doubt concerning addition is to perform the two sajdahs of sahw. The narration is significant in Shia fiqh for prayer_rulings concerning forgetfulness and uncertainty in salat.
